```{r}
#| label: load-packages-r
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(nanoparquet)
library(glmnet)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)

# The factor zoo of lecture 10 and exercise 6
sample_start <- ymd("1973-01-01")
sample_end <- ymd("2023-12-31")
test_start <- ymd("2000-01-01")

# Penalties and folds
ridge_lambdas <- 10^seq(-7, -1, by = 0.25)
lasso_lambdas <- 10^seq(-6, -2.5, by = 0.25)
n_folds <- 5

months_per_year <- 12

# Colours of the slides, used by the figures
ku_red <- "#901A1E"
jet <- "#3d3d3d"
grey <- "#666666"
light <- "#e6e3df"
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))

source("lecture-slides/_live-poll.R")
size_poll <- "aef27-l11-sdf-size"
size_choices <- c("Fewer than 5", "5 to 20", "20 to 50", "More than 50")
```

```{r}
#| label: lecture-10-code
#| include: false
# The data and functions of lecture 10
osap_url <- paste0(
  "https://huggingface.co/datasets/OpenSourceAP/CrossSection/resolve/",
  "Data-Release-2026.10/Portfolios/Full%20Sets%20OP/PredictorLSretWide.parquet"
)
osap_file <- "data/osap_long_short_returns.parquet"
if (!file.exists(osap_file)) download.file(osap_url, osap_file, mode = "wb")
anomalies <- read_parquet(osap_file) |>
  mutate(date = floor_date(as.Date(date), "month")) |>
  filter(between(date, sample_start, sample_end)) |>
  select(date, where(\(x) !anyNA(x)))
returns <- as.matrix(select(anomalies, -date)) / 100
estimation <- anomalies$date < test_start
x_estimation <- returns[estimation, ]

sharpe_ratio <- function(x) mean(x) / sd(x) * sqrt(months_per_year)
portfolio_sharpe <- function(weights) {
  c(
    estimation = sharpe_ratio(returns[estimation, ] %*% weights),
    test = sharpe_ratio(returns[!estimation, ] %*% weights)
  )
}
ridge_weights <- function(x, lambda) {
  solve(crossprod(x) + nrow(x) * lambda * diag(ncol(x)), colSums(x))
}
lasso_weights <- function(x, lambda) {
  fit <- glmnet(
    x, rep(1, nrow(x)), lambda = lambda, intercept = FALSE, standardize = FALSE,
    control = list(thresh = 1e-12)
  )
  as.vector(coef(fit))[-1]
}

# A penalty in text: 10⁻⁴ or 3.2 × 10⁻⁴
penalty_text <- function(x) {
  exponent <- floor(log10(x) + 1e-9)
  mantissa <- signif(x / 10^exponent, 2)
  power <- paste0("10", chartr("-0123456789", "⁻⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹", exponent))
  if (mantissa == 1) power else paste(mantissa, "×", power)
}

market <- read_parquet("data/factors_ff3_monthly.parquet") |>
  filter(between(date, sample_start, sample_end))
market_sharpe <- c(
  estimation = sharpe_ratio(market$mkt_excess[market$date < test_start]),
  test = sharpe_ratio(market$mkt_excess[market$date >= test_start])
)
equal_sharpe <- portfolio_sharpe(rep(1 / ncol(returns), ncol(returns)))
plug_in_sharpe <- portfolio_sharpe(ridge_weights(x_estimation, 0))
ridge_path <- map(ridge_lambdas, \(lambda) {
  tibble(lambda = lambda, !!!portfolio_sharpe(ridge_weights(x_estimation, lambda)))
}) |>
  bind_rows()
```

## Today

- Cross-validation: choosing the penalty
- The SDF of the zoo and a prior on Sharpe ratios
- Sparse in anomalies or in principal components?

## Which penalty?

- **Lecture 10:** `r ncol(returns)` anomalies, estimation sample `r year(sample_start)`–`r year(test_start) - 1`, test sample `r year(test_start)`–`r year(sample_end)`. The plug-in portfolio falls from `r number(plug_in_sharpe[["estimation"]], 0.01)` to `r number(plug_in_sharpe[["test"]], 0.01)`
- Ridge and the lasso do better in the test sample for a wide range of $\lambda$: with ridge, between `r number(min(ridge_path$test), 0.01)` and `r number(max(ridge_path$test), 0.01)`
- The best $\lambda$ in the test sample is no option: an investor in 1999 does not know the test sample

::: {.highlight}
**Today:** choose $\lambda$ with the estimation sample only, and give the penalty an economic meaning
:::

# Cross-validation

## Cross-validation for time series

```{r}
#| label: plot-folds
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.2
# Five consecutive blocks of the estimation sample, as in the code below
fold_id <- ceiling(seq_len(sum(estimation)) / (sum(estimation) / n_folds))
fold_years <- anomalies$date[estimation] |> year() |> split(fold_id)
fold_plan <- expand_grid(fold = seq_len(n_folds), block = seq_len(n_folds)) |>
  mutate(
    start = map_dbl(block, \(b) min(fold_years[[b]])),
    end = map_dbl(block, \(b) max(fold_years[[b]]) + 1),
    role = if_else(fold == block, "Validation", "Estimation")
  ) |>
  bind_rows(tibble(
    fold = seq_len(n_folds), block = 0, start = year(test_start), end = year(sample_end) + 1,
    role = "Test, never used for tuning"
  ))

ggplot(fold_plan, aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = fold - 0.4, ymax = fold + 0.4, fill = role)) +
  geom_rect(color = "white") +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq_len(n_folds), labels = paste("Fold", seq_len(n_folds))) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Estimation" = "#b3b3b3", "Validation" = ku_red, "Test, never used for tuning" = light),
    breaks = c("Estimation", "Validation", "Test, never used for tuning")
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid = element_blank())
```

- Each penalty is judged on data it was not estimated on: `r n_folds` consecutive blocks of the estimation sample, each one the validation block once
- Months are not shuffled into the folds: neighbouring months share news and volatility, so shuffling would leak information into the validation block
- The test sample stays untouched until the very end

## Cross-validation in code

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: cross-validation-r
# Five consecutive blocks: estimate on four, Sharpe ratio on the fifth
folds <- ceiling(seq_len(nrow(x_estimation)) / (nrow(x_estimation) / n_folds))

cv_sharpe <- function(fit_weights, lambda) {
  map_dbl(seq_len(n_folds), \(k) {
    weights <- fit_weights(x_estimation[folds != k, ], lambda)
    sharpe_ratio(x_estimation[folds == k, ] %*% weights)
  }) |>
    mean(na.rm = TRUE)
}

ridge_cv <- map_dbl(ridge_lambdas, \(lambda) cv_sharpe(ridge_weights, lambda))
ridge_lambda <- ridge_lambdas[which.max(ridge_cv)]
lasso_cv <- map_dbl(lasso_lambdas, \(lambda) cv_sharpe(lasso_weights, lambda))
lasso_lambda <- lasso_lambdas[which.max(lasso_cv)]
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: cross-validation-py
#| eval: false
# Five consecutive blocks: estimate on four, Sharpe ratio on the fifth
folds = np.ceil(np.arange(1, len(x_estimation) + 1) / (len(x_estimation) / n_folds))


def cv_sharpe(fit_weights, lam):
    sharpes = [sharpe_ratio(x_estimation[folds == k] @ fit_weights(x_estimation[folds != k], lam))
               for k in range(1, n_folds + 1)]
    return np.nanmean(sharpes)


ridge_cv = [cv_sharpe(ridge_weights, lam) for lam in ridge_lambdas]
ridge_lambda = ridge_lambdas[np.argmax(ridge_cv)]
lasso_cv = [cv_sharpe(lasso_weights, lam) for lam in lasso_lambdas]
lasso_lambda = lasso_lambdas[np.argmax(lasso_cv)]
```
:::

```{r}
#| label: chosen-penalties
#| include: false
ridge_sharpe <- portfolio_sharpe(ridge_weights(x_estimation, ridge_lambda))
lasso_chosen_weights <- lasso_weights(x_estimation, lasso_lambda)
lasso_sharpe <- portfolio_sharpe(lasso_chosen_weights)
```

`x_estimation`, `sharpe_ratio()`, `ridge_weights()` and `lasso_weights()` as in lecture 10. Chosen: $\lambda$ = `r penalty_text(ridge_lambda)` for ridge (test Sharpe ratio `r number(ridge_sharpe[["test"]], 0.01)`), `r penalty_text(lasso_lambda)` for the lasso (`r sum(lasso_chosen_weights != 0)` anomalies, `r number(lasso_sharpe[["test"]], 0.01)`)

# The SDF of the zoo

## Whiteboard: the SDF of the zoo

::: {.box}
Find the SDF $m = 1 - b'(F - E[F])$ that prices all anomaly returns $F$: $E[m\,F] = 0$
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$
E[m\,F] = \mu - E\big[F(F - \mu)'\big]\,b = \mu - \Sigma b = 0 \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad b = \Sigma^{-1}\mu
$$

- The SDF's loadings are the weights of the mean-variance efficient portfolio (lecture 6): estimating the SDF and choosing the best portfolio of the zoo are the same problem
- Each anomaly is a characteristic-managed portfolio, a long-short sort (lectures 7 and 8). $b$ says how much each characteristic matters for prices
:::

## Whiteboard: a prior on Sharpe ratios

::: {.box}
Kozak, Nagel & Santosh (2020): before seeing the data, $\mu \sim N\big(0, \tfrac{\kappa^2}{\tau}\Sigma^2\big)$ with $\tau = \text{tr}(\Sigma)$. What does this prior say about the maximum Sharpe ratio $\mu'\Sigma^{-1}\mu$?
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$
E\big[\mu'\Sigma^{-1}\mu\big] = \kappa^2 \qquad \hat b = (\Sigma + \lambda I)^{-1}\hat\mu \quad \text{with} \quad \lambda = \frac{\tau}{\kappa^2 T}
$$

- The posterior mean of $b$ is a ridge estimator: the penalty of lecture 10 is a prior about how large Sharpe ratios can be
- Prior means are small for principal components with little variance: a large Sharpe ratio from a low-variance combination of anomalies is implausible
:::

## The prior behind cross-validation

```{r}
#| label: implied-kappa
#| include: false
# The annual maximum Sharpe ratio that the prior expects for each penalty
tau <- sum(diag(cov(x_estimation)))
implied_kappa <- function(lambda) sqrt(tau / (lambda * nrow(x_estimation)) * months_per_year)
kappa_path <- ridge_path |>
  mutate(kappa = implied_kappa(lambda), cv = ridge_cv) |>
  filter(lambda > 0)

# Ridge on second moments and the posterior mean point in the same direction
covariance <- cov(x_estimation) * (nrow(x_estimation) - 1) / nrow(x_estimation)
posterior_weights <- solve(covariance + ridge_lambda * diag(ncol(returns)), colMeans(x_estimation))
same_direction <- cor(posterior_weights, as.vector(ridge_weights(x_estimation, ridge_lambda)))
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-kappa
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.2
kappa_path |>
  select(kappa, cv, estimation, test) |>
  pivot_longer(-kappa, names_to = "sample", values_to = "sharpe") |>
  mutate(sample = factor(
    case_match(sample, "cv" ~ "Cross-validation (estimation sample)", "estimation" ~ "Estimation 1973–1999", "test" ~ "Test 2000–2023"),
    levels = c("Estimation 1973–1999", "Cross-validation (estimation sample)", "Test 2000–2023")
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = kappa, y = sharpe, color = sample)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = implied_kappa(ridge_lambda), linetype = "dashed", color = grey) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#b3b3b3", jet, ku_red)) +
  labs(x = "Maximum Sharpe ratio the prior expects (κ, annualized)", y = "Sharpe ratio", color = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

- The cross-validated $\lambda$ = `r penalty_text(ridge_lambda)` means a prior that expects a maximum Sharpe ratio of about **`r number(implied_kappa(ridge_lambda), 0.1)`** a year: still optimistic, but far below the plug-in's `r number(plug_in_sharpe[["estimation"]], 0.1)`
- Same portfolio as ridge on the regression of lecture 10 (correlation of the weights `r number(same_direction, 0.01)`): the prior is the reason for the penalty, not a new method

# Sparse in anomalies or in principal components?

## Principal components as portfolios

- Kozak, Nagel & Santosh: an SDF with a few anomalies prices badly; an SDF with a few **principal components** of the anomalies prices well
- A principal component is a portfolio of all anomalies: rotate the returns, run the lasso on the components, rotate the weights back

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```{r}
#| label: pc-lasso-r
pc_lasso_weights <- function(x, lambda) {
  components <- eigen(cov(x), symmetric = TRUE)$vectors
  components %*% lasso_weights(x %*% components, lambda)
}

pc_lasso_cv <- map_dbl(lasso_lambdas, \(lambda) cv_sharpe(pc_lasso_weights, lambda))
pc_lasso_lambda <- lasso_lambdas[which.max(pc_lasso_cv)]
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: pc-lasso-py
#| eval: false
def pc_lasso_weights(x, lam):
    _, components = np.linalg.eigh(np.cov(x, rowvar=False))
    return components @ lasso_weights(x @ components, lam)


pc_lasso_cv = [cv_sharpe(pc_lasso_weights, lam) for lam in lasso_lambdas]
pc_lasso_lambda = lasso_lambdas[np.argmax(pc_lasso_cv)]
```
:::

The principal components come from the estimation folds only, also inside the cross-validation

## Sparse in what?

```{r}
#| label: sparsity-paths
#| include: false
components_estimation <- eigen(cov(x_estimation), symmetric = TRUE)$vectors
sparsity <- bind_rows(
  map(lasso_lambdas, \(lambda) {
    weights <- lasso_weights(x_estimation, lambda)
    tibble(inputs = "Anomalies", lambda = lambda, kept = sum(weights != 0), !!!portfolio_sharpe(weights))
  }),
  map(lasso_lambdas, \(lambda) {
    pc_weights <- lasso_weights(x_estimation %*% components_estimation, lambda)
    tibble(
      inputs = "Principal components", lambda = lambda, kept = sum(pc_weights != 0),
      !!!portfolio_sharpe(components_estimation %*% pc_weights)
    )
  })
)
pc_chosen <- sparsity |> filter(inputs == "Principal components", lambda == pc_lasso_lambda)
anomaly_chosen <- sparsity |> filter(inputs == "Anomalies", lambda == lasso_lambda)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-sparsity
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.2
chosen <- bind_rows(anomaly_chosen, pc_chosen)
ggplot(sparsity, aes(x = kept, y = test, color = inputs)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_point(data = chosen, size = 5, shape = 21, stroke = 1.3, fill = NA) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(jet, ku_red)) +
  labs(
    x = "Anomalies or principal components with a weight", y = "Sharpe ratio 2000–2023",
    color = "Lasso on", caption = "Circles: penalty chosen by cross-validation"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

- On our zoo, the components are **not** sparser: `r pc_chosen$kept` components give `r number(pc_chosen$test, 0.01)` in the test sample, `r anomaly_chosen$kept` anomalies give `r number(anomaly_chosen$test, 0.01)`
- Neither is sparse: a good SDF of the zoo needs dozens of anomalies or components, not a handful

## Beyond one SDF: averaging over models

- Every penalty, every sparse set of anomalies is one model of the SDF. Which one is right is uncertain, too
- **Bayesian model averaging** (Bryzgalova, Huang & Julliard, 2023): weight every combination of factors by its posterior probability and average the SDFs
- Their finding: no small set of factors dominates; the averaged SDF is dense, in line with the scoreboard

## Scoreboard

```{r}
#| label: scoreboard
#| echo: false
tibble(
  Portfolio = c(
    "Market", "1/N over all anomalies", "Plug-in mean-variance",
    "Ridge (prior on Sharpe ratios)",
    "Lasso on anomalies",
    "Lasso on principal components"
  ),
  Inputs = c(
    "Market", paste(ncol(returns), "anomalies"), paste(ncol(returns), "anomalies"),
    paste(ncol(returns), "anomalies"), paste(anomaly_chosen$kept, "anomalies"),
    paste(pc_chosen$kept, "components")
  ),
  estimation = c(
    market_sharpe[["estimation"]], equal_sharpe[["estimation"]], plug_in_sharpe[["estimation"]],
    ridge_sharpe[["estimation"]], anomaly_chosen$estimation, pc_chosen$estimation
  ),
  test = c(
    market_sharpe[["test"]], equal_sharpe[["test"]], plug_in_sharpe[["test"]],
    ridge_sharpe[["test"]], anomaly_chosen$test, pc_chosen$test
  )
) |>
  mutate(across(c(estimation, test), \(x) number(x, 0.01))) |>
  rename(`Sharpe ratio 1973–1999` = estimation, `Sharpe ratio 2000–2023` = test)
```

- Every penalty chosen by cross-validation in the estimation sample
- **Lecture 12:** a few factors from the principal components, chosen for their premium instead of their variance
